config_name: XPS 16 — Core Ultra 7 358H (Arc), 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 16" 3.2K OLED touch

specs.ports: 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) with DP 2.1 + PD, universal audio jack
specs.keyboard_notes: Backlit keyboard, zero-lattice design, Gorilla Glass 3 palmrest

battery.notes: 70Wh. OLED tier loses ~1-1.5h vs the 2K LCD per CNET line testing; ~10-11h real-world mixed.

reviews.quote: the XPS 16 is a fantastic laptop befitting of the premium XPS name

praises: 3.2K OLED touch is the screen this line deserves — CNET highlights the 3.2K OLED option as the XPS 16's showpiece
OLED tier is actually LIGHTER (1.65 kg) than the LCD tier (1.74 kg) and thinner (14.62 mm)
Owners cite smooth video editing and a 'vivid OLED display' as the top reasons to buy (dell.ca review summary)
120Hz + true blacks makes dark-room work and HDR video excellent
16-core 358H + 32GB handles creator workloads without a dGPU brick
complaints: CAD $4,800 with no discrete GPU — 'RTX-level price without RTX GPU' (CNET)
No upgrade path: RAM and SSD both fixed (CNET con)
Glossy OLED reflects more in bright rooms than the matte-ish LCD
USB-C-only ports; creators still need a dock for SD/HDMI

design_philosophy: The OLED tier is the config the 2026 XPS 16 was designed around: 'the ultimate creator's canvas' — a 3.2K OLED in a 14.62 mm chassis that stays lighter than its own LCD sibling. It trades battery and price for the best display in any thin 16-inch Windows laptop.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 16 (2026) 8.0 anchor (reviewed with 3.2K OLED option per CNET). OLED delta vs LCD tier: screen_quality 6.5→9.0, readability_dark →9.5, readability_bright −0.5 (gloss), battery −1, creative_work +1.5, portability +0.5 (1.65 kg).
